Hi Joshua,

These functions are not directly compiled with the ctmm package, so loading each of the scripts in the repository as you mentioned would be the correct way to use them. Going through the R scripts using the source() function should load in all the necessary functions into your current environment, but if that fails, you can always just manually run through all the lines in each of the scripts.

That being said, I will refine some of the guides, as well as add in some extra functionalities that have not yet been published within the next week or two, which may help. I will notify everyone here once that has been reflected in the GitHub repository.

messages.subject: Inconsistent grid resolutions for overlap (single telemetry object and fit list)
messages.subject_clean: Inconsistent grid resolutions for overlap (single telemetry object and fit list)
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I know there have already been a few threads on this, but I believe this is a somewhat unique issue.

I am attempting to get overlap values for ADKEs, and am getting the dreaded:
"Error in grid.intersection(UD) : Inconsistent grid resolutions."

Unlike in previous threads though, all individuals are from the same telemetry object, and akde() is being run on a single list of fitted models for these individuals. This is my standard approach and I've not run into issues previously. The only tweak is that I am running this in parallel on RStudio Server, but I can't see how that would impact things.

I guess my question is whether there are other issues that can cause one to have inconsistent grid resolutions, even when all animals are in the same telemetry object, and all the fitted models are based on that telemetry object. Code example is below, and I encounter no other errors. Objects all summarize and plot fine. I initially thought this might be caused by having two groups of animals that were separated by a large distance. But this example below includes only individuals living in the same area. And I'm actually having this same issue with another dataset now. I"m starting to wonder if I need to force the grid as suggested by Allie Anderson (Nov 19, 2025) as a general rule whenever I''m aiming to estimate overlap?

I'm OK to try to that, but did not anticipate needing to add that to my workflow since I haven't needed to do it in the past at all. Thanks for any suggestions!

Joe

"tapir_tel_n" is a single telemetry object with 6 individuals.

tapir_fits_n <-
  mclapply(seq_along(tapir_tel_n),
           function(i) {

             my_tel <- tapir_tel_n[[i]]

             my_guess <- ctmm.guess(my_tel,
                                    CTMM = ctmm(error = TRUE),
                                    interactive = FALSE)

             ctmm.select(my_tel,
                         my_guess,
                         verbose = FALSE)
           },
           mc.cores = 6,
           mc.preschedule = FALSE)

tapir_akde_n <- mclapply(seq_along(tapir_tel_n),
                       function(i) {

                         akde(tapir_tel_n[[i]],
                              CTMM = tapir_fits_n[[i]],
                              weights = TRUE)},
                       mc.cores = 6,
                       mc.preschedule = FALSE)

north_overlap <- overlap(tapir_akde_n,
                       level = 0.95,
                       debias = TRUE)

Error in grid.intersection(UD) : Inconsistent grid resolutions.

messages.subject: Re: Sliding window analysis function
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I have updated the GitHub repository to include a new argument in the slide function called "release". By setting release = TRUE, users can now examine trends in terms of days elapsed since release/tracking using the slide() function. This can also work with populations where different individuals were released or began tagging at different times. The example_usage script now includes this "release = TRUE" case. I have also modified the function to take in entire population datasets even if there are gaps or periods with only one individual with available tracking data. For each window, the function will only use the individuals with data available during that window.

Please feel free to ask any questions or point out any issues regarding these sliding window function.

Best,
Nozomu

messages.subject: RSF error
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris,

I’m using rsf.select() and am running into an error code for a handful of my individuals. The error suggests that there are NA values for some sampled points. I confirmed that the rasters adequately cover the akde, so NAs are not being extracted from the raster.

I looked through the code for the rsf.select() and rsf.fit() functions to try and understand what is happening.

If I understand correctly, rsf.select() tries various models using the parameters from the previous model to inform the next model. What seems to be happening is that, in some cases, a model ends up with estimates of NaN or Inf for various parameters, and importantly for mu. This results in NaNs for x and y in DATA within rsf.select() and triggers the warning.

Does this interpretation sound correct? If so, do you have a recommendation for handling this? Would it be reasonable to select the best performing model from the ones that did work and didn’t result in NaNs or Inf?

Thank you for your help!

-Stella

messages.subject: Erroneous overlap values?
messages.body_plain:
Hello all, hope you are well. I've been fitting joint AKDEs via the usual method:

AKDES <- akde(vultures_reproj[c(k,j)], FITS_object[c(k,j)], weights = TRUE, dt.plot = FALSE)

where vultures_reproj is a list of telemetry objects all on a shared assigned projection and FITS_object is a list of the individual ctmm models with identical index values to the vultures_reproj list.

This successfully fits the joint AKDEs on a shared grid in preparation for use of the overlap function. I'm fitting a large number of pairs and in some cases they seem to have no issue. However, one pair (or more) is definitely giving what I interpret to be impossible, with very high confidence interval values coming out of the overlap function (low: 0.89, est 0.95, high: 0.98) despite these two distributions possessing no physical overlap in space, separated by at least a few hundred kilometers completely. Is there any clear possible step at which I may have gone wrong here?

Thank you for any help or guidance you can offer! Can provide reproducible code privately if needed.

Best,
Storm

messages.subject: Variogram oscillations in shorebird GPS data
messages.subject_clean: Variogram oscillations in shorebird GPS data
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I have some questions about my interesting variograms in the attached zip folder.

The variograms are of GPS tracking data from migratory shorebirds in a dynamic intertidal coastline.

12-hourly cycles appear evidence in all individuals, deemed due to foraging and roost commutes (noting the periodograms have red diagnostic points which suggest that may be an artefactual periodicity).

I can see clear 2-weekly amplitude changes in svf. These make sense, as the larger amplitude would represent spring tide (larger low-high tide difference means further travel to optimal tide height foraging places), and the smaller ones likely amplitudes represent neap tide (birds move shorter distances from central place to get optimal tidal height for foraging). Can such amplitude changes be expressly modelled in, or do I need to segment the data in 2-week blocks?

I think that each individual will require its own PROTO model. Could anyone please provide some advice about how to model these oscillations?

Below is a variogram with a model for UUN. This was the second model selected by AICc - the winning model had no 2-weekly harmonic and didn't look right. And in any event, is
it acceptable that the amplitude changes were not modelled?
My initial assessment is as follows:

UUN:
- slight mean cycle (2 weeks)
- amplitude cycle (2 weeks)

UUR:
- mean cycle over 5 months (entire non-breeding residency period)
- amplitude cycle (2 weeks)

VDB:
- No period - except maybe a 12-hourly cycle as with the others

VDD:
- mean cycle (2 weeks)

VDS:
- 12-hourly periodic mean

VPW:
- Periodic mean (12-hour and 2 week harmonics)

VPY:
- stable mean
- amplitude cycle (2 weeks)

VPZ:
- 12-hourly periodic mean
- 2-weekly amplitude cycle
- final ~1 month either a lower sampling schedule or a separate premigration behavior (likely needs to be segmented out for separate analysis?)

Below is a variogram with a model for UUN. This was the second model selected by AICc - the winning model had no 2-weekly harmonic and didn't look right. And in any event, is
it acceptable that the amplitude changes were not modelled?
I would love to hear any help from the ctmm brain's trust. Any insights will be greatly appreciated!!

Cheers,
Alex Brunswick

messages.subject: GPS data from bluetooth trackers
messages.body_plain:
QS

Hello all,

I am doing a study on my university cats' home ranges. The tracker we are using is Damien Farine's Bluetooth Low-energy (BLE) beacons. The tags transmit a signal that can be detected by an Apple device. The phone receiving the signal captures a location from its own GPS and uploads the identity of the tag and its location to Apple's iCloud, which essentially makes up my data.

Here is an example of how the data is collected:

For finding home range of each cat, I am using R package ctmm to calculate Autocorrelated Kernel Density Estimator (AKDE). Before, I only removed ACCs > 100 which left me with ~14 000 rows of observations for each cat over the duration of 2.5 months, which ctmm was not able to handle. Hence, I wish to find a way to thin out the data (make it temporally less dense, since the smallest time interval I have currently is 1 second) while accounting for accuracy/ error estimates.

What I did to solve the issue:

Duplicated timestamps
Duplicated location points
ACC > 50 (Accuracy estimator in metres)

This left me with ~3000 rows of data for each cat.

Using ctmm R package to derive home range from weighted AKDE (wAKDE) & AKDE:

```

data(summer_cat)

putu <- summer_cat$NUS003

GUESS <- ctmm.guess(putu,interactive=FALSE) # automated model guess

M.OUF <- ctmm.fit(putu,GUESS)

wAKDE <- akde(putu,M.OUF,weights=TRUE)

AKDE <- akde(putu,M.OUF)

#Plot

EXT <- extent(AKDE,level=0.95) #DOP is missing. Assumed to be 1.

#wAKDE
```

The issue here is that the estimate of home range seem to be giving me a circle, when there are clear contours to the data points.

My questions:

How do I thin out my data? Other than removing obvious outliers, I tried to filter the data by creating new cluster points (in R I attempted to create a function to cluster points within a certain stationary threshold, and the centroid of this point would be the new point)
How do I account for inaccuracies, especially because this technology is quite new and the only accuracy estimator I have is ACC which I am unsure of how to calibrate it so that I can account for it in the ctmm package.
Why is the home range a circle?
Should I be using AKDE to find home range or BBMM (Brownian bridge movement model)? BBMM which is better equipped to deal with auto-correlated and clustered position data than KDE home range estimator commonly used in wildlife studies. Specifically, BBMM allows estimation of probabilistic space-use, while accounting for position error and the uncertainty about paths taken between consecutive positions.

Apologies for the information dump, I am relatively new to movement ecology and R so any advice/ corrections for any of the points mentioned will be greatly appreciated. :)

Hi ctmm team and community,

I am attempting to fit an integrated Resource Selection Function (ctmm::rsf.fit()) for a segmented individual dataset (cl_s2) using two continuous environmental predictors (elevation, dist_to_water) and one categorical land use / land cover raster (lulc_code).

Following the package documentation for categorical variables (raster::as.factor()), I attached a Raster Attribute Table (RAT) to the factor raster. However, when executing rsf.fit() with the reference argument specified, the function throws the following error: Error in reference[NAME] <- REF : replacement has length zero

Before running rsf.fit(), I verified that:

All rasters are fully loaded in system RAM (raster::inMemory() evaluates to TRUE).

Telemetry data and raster layers share the exact same spatial projection.

Zero missing values (NAs) exist at telemetry locations.

The RAT table is structured as a strict 2-column data frame (ID, lulc_code), and "Forest" is confirmed present in Column 2.
Questions

Is there a specific format required for the S4 RasterLayer RAT slot so that rsf.fit() can extract the factor level names during reference indexing?

Versions of the R and packages:
R version 4.6.0 (2026-04-24 ucrt)
'ctmm' version 1.3.0
‘raster’ version 3.6-32

I am uploading the document containing console for reference.  I really appreciate any suggestions or help in resolving this. Thank you for developing such a fantastic package and for ongoing support to the community.
